```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE)
library(tidyverse)
#Removing NAs
Data = suppressWarnings(read.csv("data.csv")) %>% 
  drop_na()
```

### Introduction

I used data from Anki, an open source digital flashcard application, to see how my study habits relate to my actual grades for each exam. 

  * **Daily_Ave** - Represents the number of daily average flashcards repetitions per set.
   * **Studied **- The number of days spent studying for an exam.
   * **Difficulty **- Perceived difficulty of the exam

### Relationship between exam grade and daily average flashcards 
```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
dailyave_grade <- lm(Grade ~ Daily_Ave, data = Data)
summary(dailyave_grade)
```

### Relationship between grades and daily average flashcards, days studied, and difficulty
```{r}
#summary table
summary(lm(Grade ~ Daily_Ave + Studied + Difficulty, data = Data))
```


```{r}
#Correlation Plot
ggplot(Data, aes(Data$Daily_Ave, Data$Grade)) + geom_point()+
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE, method = "lm") +
  ylab("Exam Grade (Percent)") +
  xlab("Daily Average Flashcards")+
  ggtitle("Correlation Between Daily Average Flashcards and Grade (%)")


```


### Correlation Between Number of Days Studied and Grade (%)
```{r}
#r correlation coefficient
x = cor(Data$Studied, Data$Grade)
cat("Our correlation coefficient is: ", x)
```

#### Plotting this correlation
```{r}
ggplot(Data, aes(Data$Studied, Data$Grade)) + geom_point()+
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE, method = "lm") +
  ylab("Exam Grade") +
  xlab("Number of Days Studied")+
  ggtitle("Correlation Between Number of Days Studied and Grade (%)") 
```

#### Separating the correlation plot by class
```{r}
ggplot(Data, aes(Data$Studied, Data$Grade, color = Class)) +
    geom_point()+
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE, method = "lm") +
  #facet_wrap(~Class)+ optional if you wanna see individual plots
    ylab("Exam Grade") +
  xlab("Number of Days Studied")+
  ggtitle("Correlation Between Number of Days Studied and Grade (%) by Class")


```

**Need at least 30 points, preliminary analysis shows no correlation**

```{r}
ggplot(Data, aes(x = Studied)) + 
  geom_histogram()

```

### Future Directions: 
 * Look for interactions between days studied & exam grade and flashcard numbers.
  * Correct for other covarients. Each class has different average scores/distribution of scores. Keep track of subject of class/department/level of class may give a better sense of what is actually predictive of percentage score.
 *  You could compare quartiles/madgrade/ percentile to measure how well you did in classes
